text.paragraph: New primary care visit for chronic back, pelvic, and right leg pain on long-term opioid therapy. tr.td: Poliomyelitis at age six in 1913, leaving the right leg thinner, shorter, and less developed, with the foot turned outward
Congenital spinal anomaly (spina bifida) proposed retrospectively; not established

Bus and streetcar collision on September 17, 1925: pelvic fracture from a handrail injury through the hip, three spinal fractures, fractured collarbone and two ribs, dislocated right shoulder, and eleven fractures of the right leg with a dislocated foot
Many operations after the accident, some with long convalescences, and about 25 different corsets for posture

tr.td: New primary care visit for chronic back, pelvic, and right leg pain on long-term opioid therapy
Physical medicine and rehabilitation consultation for a multimodal rehabilitation plan
Four-week chronic pain follow-up with the first opioid dose reduction
Six-week chronic pain review of function, mood, and the opioid taper
Physical medicine and rehabilitation referral for a multimodal rehabilitation plan: exercise therapy, bracing and orthotic review, a shoe lift for the leg-length difference, and function goals
Nonopioid treatment first: duloxetine titrated to 60 mg daily, scheduled acetaminophen up to 3 g a day, and topical diclofenac for the ankle

Opioid risk mitigation: review benefits and harms together, check the prescription drug monitoring program, urine drug test with consent, prescribe naloxone 4 mg nasal spray and teach a family member, and avoid benzodiazepines and other sedatives
Collaborative, gradual opioid taper of about 10% of the dose a month, paused if pain or function worsens; never stop opioids abruptly
Physical therapy twice weekly with graded exercise and aquatic therapy, pain neuroscience education, and cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic pain

Measure pain and function with the PEG at every visit and depressive symptoms with the PHQ-9 every two to four weeks; complete a structured safety assessment if the PHQ-9 reaches 10 or item 9 is positive
Check ALT periodically on regular acetaminophen, and replete vitamin D
Improve the PEG score by at least 30% from baseline
PEG fell from 7.3 to 5.3 by the six-week review, a 27% improvement; goal continued
Stand at the easel for 30 minutes at a time by the six-week review
Stands 25 to 30 minutes at the easel with the shoe lift
First opioid dose reduction, agreed by the patient, without loss of function
Reduced from 60 to 52.5 MME a day at the four-week visit; PEG and standing tolerance improved at the six-week review
Naloxone in the home with a family member trained to use it
Naloxone nasal spray dispensed; spouse taught at the first visit
